subject: general
question: A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it amount to 9 times of itself?
solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 10 years.

**Concept Used:**

Amount = P(1+(r)/(100))^n

**Calculation:**

When the sum of money gets tripled in 10 years,

Amount = 3P

⇒ 3P = P(1+(r)/(100))¹⁰

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))¹⁰ = (3P)/(P) = 3 → (1)

Now, when the amount required is 9 times of itself,

Amount = 9P

⇒ 9P = P(1+(r)/(100))^n

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))^n = (9P)/(P) = 9 = 3² → (2)

Putting the value of 3 from equation (1) into equation (2), we get

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))^n = ({(1+(r)/(100))}¹⁰)²

⇒ (1+(r)/(100))^n = (1+(r)/(100))¹⁰times ²

Equating the powers, we get

⇒ n = 20 years

**Therefore, the required time in which the amount becomes 9 times of itself is 20 years.**
